# MotherTongueIndex

> A free, open, CPU-only tool that measures how efficiently the tokenizers of 28
> mainstream large language models encode text in any language, anchored to
> English. It reports the token cost of a language versus English and the
> reasoning-capability impact of tokenization. A subproject of Project Bornomala.

## What it answers

- How many more tokens does a given language cost than English on a given model?
  (the "versus English" or xEN ratio)
- Which tokenizers are efficient or inefficient for a given script?
- How much effective context, and therefore reasoning capacity at fixed budget,
  does a language lose to tokenization overhead?

## Key facts (verifiable, reproducible)

- Every mainstream tokenizer is optimised for English; non-Latin and complex
  (Indic, abugida) scripts pay a token tax.
- The tax is generation-dependent: on OpenAI's tokenizers, Bengali fertility
  falls from 8.40 tokens/word (cl100k, GPT-4) to 1.90 (o200k, GPT-4o); Hindi
  falls from about 5.0x English to about 1.5x. Tokenization, not the language,
  drives the cost.
- Claude, Gemini, and Grok have no public tokenizer, so their counts are
  labelled estimates, never presented as measured.

## Method

- Exact tokenization via OpenAI tiktoken and Hugging Face tokenizers.
- Metrics: fertility (tokens per whitespace word), single-token retention rate,
  bytes per token, grapheme clusters per token (Unicode UAX #29), and the
  versus-English ratio anchored on a fixed reference and on parallel text.
- Capability impact is derived from effective-context loss and clearly separated
  from the measured reasoning probe.
